_comment: Fragment 85 — D-129: a routed packet that went stale under its own feet, and a new gap checked for duplication before being recorded. Merged 2026-08-25.

nodes.label: A Routed Business-Decision Packet Went Stale Under Its Own Feet
nodes.description: A packet already sent to a decision-maker referenced a value by its bare number, and two later passes named and architecturally resolved part of that same number's meaning without the packet being told.
nodes.rationale: A packet is a snapshot handed to someone outside the repository's edit cycle, so it cannot self-update the way an internal document can. Checking whether an already-routed ask still matches current terminology is a distinct propagation surface from checking whether internal documents agree with each other, and it was overlooked by every check built for the latter.

nodes.label: A New Gap Checked Against Its Neighbors Before Being Recorded
nodes.description: Before adding a newly opened gap to the tracking table, its relationship to two topically adjacent gaps was verified rather than assumed, confirming it named a distinct upstream question rather than restating either.
nodes.rationale: An instruction to avoid duplicates is only honored by checking, not by asserting distinctness after the fact. The check found the new item was a genuine precondition of the two neighbors rather than an overlap, which is the difference between adding tracked scope and adding tracked noise.
